verdict.rationale: Statsig's environments guide says SDKs evaluate gates, configs, and experiments differently in development and staging than in production. Environment-specific SDK keys decide which rule sets each SDK downloads, and data is kept separate across dev, staging, and prod, which covers independent per-environment flag states and scoped keys. Target apps add further key-level scoping of which configs are visible. Missing for 10: detailed docs on creating and managing custom environments and per-environment toggle workflows, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of environment isolation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: evaluate feature gates, dynamic configs, and experiments differently in non-production environments like development or staging
environment-specific SDK keys determining which rule sets download and separated development/staging/production data
Specifying a target app for your client key and linking only client-specific configs to it keeps those configs from being visible.
